**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 02:23  
[FACT] User is creating a scale model of the Titanic.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for advice on creating realistic water effects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended techniques for creating a realistic ocean surface include resin pouring, acrylic gel, water effects medium, and Envirotex Lite.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested YouTube tutorials: "Model Ship Water Effects" by Model Shipwrights, "Titanic Diorama Water Effects" by Model Builder's Guide, and "Water Effects for Model Ships" by The Model Maker.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended online forums: Model Shipwrights Forum and The Model Making Forum.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested books: "Model Ship Building" by David Griffiths and "Scale Modeler" magazine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided tips for realism: study reference images, experiment with techniques, add sea foam or whitecaps, and be patient.  
[FACT] User has seen videos on YouTube about using resin for water effects but has never tried it before.  
[PREFERENCE] User is concerned about removing air bubbles when working with resin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Explained that a pressure pot is useful for removing air bubbles but provided alternative methods: mixing and pouring techniques, vacuum chamber, heat and vibration, bubble releasers, torch or flame, patience and time, and using bubble-free resin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended beginner-friendly epoxy resins: West System 105/205, J-B Weld epoxy, Loctite Epoxy Instant Mix, ArtResin, and Smooth-On Epoxy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested mixing resin and hardener in a well-ventilated area, using a clean container, and following the recommended mixing ratio (1:1 for beginners).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided tips for mixing resin: mix thoroughly, scrape sides and bottom, and avoid mixing too much at once.  
[PREFERENCE] User wants to know the best way to apply resin to their model.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested methods for applying resin include using a brush, pouring technique, or other methods (details not provided in the last message).
